label: GO: tracks policy logit a1-a2; D1: high after a1 unrewarded
terms: (phase == GO) * np.tanh(choice) ;; (phase == GO) * choice ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 u") ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (tv("reward", -2) == 0)
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 0. Timing: about -0.82 at D1, about 0 at GO, saturated at -1 at D2 (D2 has no residual structure). At GO the magnitude is a graded readout of the model policy logit(a1)-logit(a2): positive when the agent is about to choose a1, negative for a2 (policy decile alone gives a 0.92 reference). It is a saturating function, so tanh(choice) plus a linear choice term fit it. The observed-history version (previous choice plus model-based stay/switch patterns) gets only about 0.63 dev, so the policy term carries most of the fit. At D1 it rises after an unrewarded a1 trial (a1 S2 u +0.74, a1 S1 u +0.32), drops slightly after any a2 trial (-0.15), and rises a little after two unrewarded trials in a row. This trial reward, state and other future variables are not used. Dev R^2 beyond timing 0.914; the all ceiling is 0.96.

issues: I reproduced the claimed test R^2 beyond timing: 0.911. Each part pulls its weight. The GO policy terms alone score 0.833, adding the two a1-unrewarded D1 terms brings it to 0.892, and the a2 term plus the two-unrewarded term bring it to 0.911.

The explanation says D1 drops 'after any a2 trial', but that is not quite true. The residual table shows a2 S2 u at +0.017 at D1, while a2 S2 r, a2 S1 r and a2 S1 u are each about -0.15 to -0.17. Misses also lists 'D1 after a2 S2 u' as under-predicted (+0.077).

There is a systematic error at GO after a2 S1 r (rare rewarded trials, where a model-based agent switches to a1). The fit under-predicts by +0.284 there: the unit stays near baseline (residual about 0.000) even though the policy favours a1. So at GO the unit is not purely the policy logit. GO after a1 S2 u is over-predicted (-0.116). Adding a GO rare-rewarded indicator only reaches 0.914 on test, so this class is small in variance terms.

The value at D1 also follows the D1 policy logit. Policy decile 8 at D1 has a residual of +0.53. Adding (phase==D1)*tanh(choice) and (phase==D1)*choice raises test R^2 from 0.911 to 0.925, so the label leaves out a small graded D1 policy component.

The worst-fit windows are long runs of unrewarded trials where D1 reads about +0.1 to +0.5 against a prediction of about -0.7. But a three-unrewarded-in-a-row D1 term adds nothing on test (0.912), and signing the previous action at GO adds nothing either (0.911). What is left looks like scatter, not a clean missing class.
